sentences.text: 15.4 Derivatives and the chain rule
sentences.say: 15.4 Derivatives and the chain rule

sentences.text: The derivative of a function is its slope at a point: how much the output changes per tiny change of the input.
sentences.say: The derivative of a function is its slope at a point: how much the output changes per tiny change of the input.

sentences.text: For a function of several inputs, the partial derivative is the slope along one of them, and the gradient is the vector of all the partial derivatives.
sentences.say: For a function of several inputs, the partial derivative is the slope along one of them, and the gradient is the vector of all the partial derivatives.

sentences.text: Gradient descent (Chapter 6) simply walks against the gradient.
sentences.say: Gradient descent (Chapter 6) simply walks against the gradient.

sentences.text: The chain rule handles a function inside a function: multiply the slope of the outer function by the slope of the inner one.
sentences.say: The chain rule handles a function inside a function: multiply the slope of the outer function by the slope of the inner one.

sentences.text: The squared error of one example is (w x - y) squared.
sentences.say: The squared error of one example is (w x minus y) squared.

sentences.text: The inner function is w x - y, with slope x with respect to w. The outer function is its square, with slope 2 (w x - y).
sentences.say: The inner function is w x minus y, with slope times with respect to w. The outer function is its square, with slope 2 (w x minus y).

sentences.text: So the derivative with respect to w is 2 (w x - y) x. This is where the 2 that cancels the 1/2 of the cost comes from (Chapter 5).
sentences.say: So the derivative with respect to w is 2 (w x minus y) x. This is where the 2 that cancels the 1/2 of the cost comes from (Chapter 5).

sentences.text: 15.5 Statistics you will use every week
sentences.say: 15.5 Statistics you will use every week

sentences.text: Mean and median: the average, and the middle value.
sentences.say: Mean and median: the average, and the middle value.

sentences.say: The median is not moved by outliers.

sentences.text: Variance and standard deviation: how spread out the values are.
sentences.say: Variance and standard deviation: how spread out the values are.

sentences.text: The standard deviation is the square root of the variance, in the original units.
sentences.say: The standard deviation is the square root of the variance, in the original units.

sentences.text: A z-score says how many standard deviations a value is from the mean (Chapter 8): a loan of 1,000 when the mean is 600 and the standard deviation is 450 has a z-score of 0.89.
sentences.say: A z-score says how many standard deviations a value is from the mean (Chapter 8): a loan of 1,000 when the mean is 600 and the standard deviation is 450 has a z-score of 0.89.

sentences.text: Correlation: from -1 to 1, how closely two columns move together in a straight-line way.
sentences.say: Correlation: from -1 to 1, how closely two columns move together in a straight-line way.

sentences.text: It never proves cause.
sentences.say: It never proves cause.

sentences.text: The normal distribution: the bell curve.

sentences.text: About 68% of values lie within 1 standard deviation of the mean, 95% within 2, and 99.7% within 3.
sentences.say: About 68 percent of values lie within 1 standard deviation of the mean, 95 percent within 2, and 99.7 percent within 3.

sentences.text: The central limit theorem: the averages of many random samples are roughly bell-shaped, whatever the shape of the original data.
sentences.say: The central limit theorem: the averages of many random samples are roughly bell-shaped, whatever the shape of the original data.

sentences.text: It is why so many statistical tests work.
sentences.say: It is why so many statistical tests work.

sentences.text: Samples and populations: you almost never see the whole population, only a sample.
sentences.say: Samples and populations: you almost never see the whole population, only a sample.

sentences.text: The law of large numbers says that sample averages settle on the truth as the sample grows.
sentences.say: The law of large numbers says that sample averages settle on the truth as the sample grows.

sentences.text: Significance and the p-value: a hypothesis test asks "if there were no real effect, how surprising would data like this be?"
sentences.say: Significance and the p-value: a hypothesis test asks "if there were no real effect, how surprising would data like this be?"

sentences.text: A small p-value (often under 0.05) means very surprising.
sentences.say: A small p-value (often under 0.05) means very surprising.

sentences.text: It does not give the probability that the effect is real.
sentences.say: It does not give the probability that the effect is real.

sentences.text: The multiple comparisons problem: test 20 unrelated things at the 5% level, and the chance that at least one looks "significant" by luck is 1 - 0.95^20, about 64%.
sentences.say: The multiple comparisons problem: test 20 unrelated things at the 5 percent level, and the chance that at least one looks "significant" by luck is 1 minus 0.95 to the power of 20, about 64 percent.

sentences.text: Fixes, such as the Bonferroni correction, demand a stricter threshold, the 5% divided by the number of tests.
sentences.say: Fixes, such as the Bonferroni correction, demand a stricter threshold, the 5 percent divided by the number of tests.

sentences.text: In machine learning the same trap appears when you try dozens of models and features and report the best one: keep a test set that you use once.

sentences.text: Common mistakes
sentences.say: Common mistakes

sentences.text: Memorizing a formula without being able to say what it is for.
sentences.say: Memorizing a formula without being able to say what it is for.

sentences.text: Reading correlation as cause, or a small p-value as "the effect is real".
sentences.say: Reading correlation as cause, or a small p-value as "the effect is real".

sentences.text: Trying many things and reporting only the best one without a fresh test.
